newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish minister sees EMU decision well received.
newsitem.headline: Swedish minister sees EMU decision well received.

text.p: Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday he expects the ruling party's view on whether Sweden should join European monetary union, to be unveiled on Tuesday, will be well received by the country's markets.

Asked by journalists after a meeting of the ruling Social Democratic Party's leadership if Tuesday's decision would worry markets, Asbrink replied: "I don't think so, but you can never be completely sure. I reckon it will be well received.

The party committee, known as VU, includes Prime Minister Goran Persson and several leading cabinet members, party officials and union leaders and will meet on Tuesday to agree the party's view on EMU membership.
Financial markets are expecting Sweden to reject membership of EMU at its proposed launch in January 1999, instead opting for membership at a later stage when public opinion is more in favour.
But Goran Jonsson, head of the Metalworkers' Union and an avowed supporter of Swedish membership, said after Friday's meeting that he was positive about Tuesday's decision.
"It's going to be a pretty good decision," he said.
